text:
Jamie: hey team—day 2 check-in. made it through the basic onboarding checklist but hit a couple blockers I can't unblock myself. TL;DR: can't get CI to pick up my runner keys, ssh to internal infra fails (permission denied), and 1Password prompts keep popping during CLI auth.

Jamie: what I did: created GitHub account, finished SSO/Okta link, installed homebrew + docker, forked the monorepo.

Jamie: blockers:
- CI: tried adding my SSH deploy key to the repo and to my user, but the `ci-runner` still fails with `Permission denied (publickey)`.
- Local SSH: `ssh git@internal.redwood` -> `Permission denied (publickey)`.
- mac keychain: every CLI call to 1Password asks for master password repeatedly; makes `op` auth flaky for scripts.

Jamie: asked Noah for infra help, filed a ticket with ops (Sam). Also happy to pair later if anyone has 15m.

Noah: hey! I can help. first quick checks: is your SSH key present in `~/.ssh` and added to the agent? run:
```
ls -la ~/.ssh
ssh-add -l || ssh-add -K ~/.ssh/id_rsa
```
On newer macs `ssh-add -K` stores in keychain; if that errors try `ssh-add --apple-use-keychain ~/.ssh/id_rsa`.

Noah: also confirm the public key you uploaded to GitHub matches `cat ~/.ssh/id_rsa.pub`. sometimes people copy the wrong file.

Jamie: ran `ls` — I have id_rsa and id_rsa.pub. `ssh-add -l` returns "The agent has no identities." ran `ssh-add -K ~/.ssh/id_rsa` and got `Could not open a connection to your authentication agent.`

Noah: ok that's why. on mac, if you're not running an agent, start one:
```
eval "$(ssh-agent -s)"
ssh-add -K ~/.ssh/id_rsa
```
Then retry `ssh -T git@github.com` and `ssh git@internal.redwood`.

Amelia: fwiw I hit the same 1Password noise — for CLI scripts we use 1password CLI session export: run `eval $(op signin your-team)` once per shell session. If it keeps asking, open 1Password desktop app and unlock once; the CLI will reuse the session token.

Sam: ops ticket #OPS-1248 opened for Jamie, linking infra logs. status: investigating CI runner auth config (looks like the runner host doesn't have the deploy key in its known_hosts/authorized_keys). I added Jamie to the ticket watchers.

Sam: quick note — if you added the key to the repo, we still need the deploy key installed on the runner VM (we don't forward personal keys). Ops will add it, ETA 2-4 hours.

Jamie: thanks! pairing offer: I can be available at 2pm PT.

Noah: cool — i'll hop on at 2 to walk through agent + runner steps. for the `Could not open a connection to your authentication agent.` message you can also run `ssh-agent zsh` then `ssh-add`.

Amelia: also check `~/.ssh/config` — we have a host alias for internal that sets `IdentitiesOnly yes` which bit me once. example snippet:
```
Host internal.redwood
  HostName internal.redwood
  User jamie
  IdentityFile ~/.ssh/id_rsa
  IdentitiesOnly yes
```
If you don't have that, add it.

IT Bot: automated: added Jamie to onboarding checklist item `CI credentials` and scheduled follow-up reminder in 3 hours. :robot_face:

Jamie: great — follow-up: after starting the agent and re-adding key, `ssh -T git@github.com` now says "Hi jamie! You've successfully authenticated" — internal still 403. waiting on ops. thanks everyone. :raised_hands:

Noah: :thumbsup: bring your laptop to the sync if ops needs a hand. also i'll drop a link to the quick fix doc in this thread in a sec.

Sam: ops update (11:23 PT): added deploy key to runner, CI test job retriggered and passed for your fork. plz try a PR and ping.

Jamie: tested a small PR — CI green. 1Password session still annoying but workable with the desktop unlock workaround.

Amelia: awesome, welcome aboard :)

Jamie: closing my blockers for now. thanks all, will ping if anything else pops up.
